description: One node in a scene file: add, read, set, duplicate, reparent or delete it, or paint TileMap cells. Any ClassDB node type or script class can be added, so a NavigationRegion2D, an AnimationTree or a Camera3D is an add with that nodeType and its properties, and another scene is instanced by an add with instancePath. A set with properties {"name": "Boss"} renames a node, and answers nodePath as its new path. A rename or a reparent carries the node paths naming the node, as the editor's rename does: NodePath values on nodes (in arrays, dictionaries, built-in resources, %unique paths) and the tracks its players' animations hold, saving a library kept in a .tres of its own. Each rewrite is listed under retargeted ({scenePath, nodePath, property or animation and track, from, to}), and under notRetargeted, with a reason, each left: a track kept in another scene or an imported file, or a value another scene gives that the move left naming nothing. The move is followed into every other .tscn that instances or inherits this scene at any depth: the editable children, values, added nodes and connections named by the old path are rewritten, since Godot finds a moved node's values by unique_id but editable children only by path and drops the values kept below them on the next save, and that scene's node paths and tracks are carried as above. A reparent also drops the node ids saved along each rewritten path, which ran through the old parent; the next save writes them again. The scenes rewritten are named under followed, and under notFollowed any left as they were, with why. A delete rewrites no path and lists under stillNaming each node path and track, here and in the scenes instancing or inheriting this one, that named the deleted node and now names nothing. A property holding a Resource takes the res:// path of one, so a texture, a material or a theme is a set like any other. Other properties the engine changed in step, as a Control's offsets with its size, come back under alsoChanged as {was, now}.A write is refused while the editor holds unsaved changes to the scene. A node this scene inherits takes values of this scene's own, and so does a node inside an instance of another scene once that instance's editableChildren is true; neither can be moved, renamed, copied or deleted, since the other scene makes it again on load. Through the editor when one serves the project; with none, a headless engine runs the editor's own tool and the answer says so under writtenBy, or readBy for a read. That engine runs every script of the file, where the editor runs only tool scripts, so what a script changes as the file loads or as a property is set is put back before anything is saved, and a file where that cannot be done, such as a scene whose script does not compile, is refused and nothing is written. Each file the written one refers to is named by its uid, as the editor names it, except a file the project's uid cache has no uid for yet (one made since the project was last scanned), which is named by path and listed under namedByPath with the call that scans it. An editor of the project that is running and has not reached this server is waited for rather than written around. Operations: add (needs nodeName): add a node of any class, or an instance of a scene; get (needs nodePath): read a node's properties, and a TileMapLayer's or TileMap's cells as set_tilemap_cells takes them, the first 1000 with cellCount for all. An instance of another scene also answers instanceOf and editableChildren, as scene_tree does; set (needs nodePath): set properties on a node, or make the children of an instance editable; give either or both; duplicate (needs nodePath, newName): copy a node and its children, beside it or under parentNodePath, answering the copy's newNodePath, parentNodePath and index; reparent (needs nodePath, newParentPath): move a node under another parent, or to another place among its siblings; delete (needs nodePath): remove a node and its children; set_tilemap_cells (needs nodePath, cells): place tiles in a TileMapLayer or TileMap.

cells.description: Cells to place. Only for op set_tilemap_cells.

atlasCoords.description: The tile in the source. Needed by every cell but an erased one.

sourceId.description: TileSet source id, or -1 to erase the cell.

editableChildren.description: set: on an instance of another scene, whether its children are editable here, as the editor's Editable Children makes them. True lets scene_node set give the nodes inside that instance values of this scene's own, which no other instance shares. An instance nested inside another takes it once the one around it has editable children. False drops every value this scene keeps for them, and every node it added below one of them. The answer names the nodes whose values went under droppedValues (they stay, with the instance's own values) and the added nodes that went under droppedNodes; a node added straight under the instance stays. The answer says editableChildren as the file now holds it. Only for op set.

includeDefaults.description: get: include properties still at their default. Default false. Only for op get.

index.description: add and reparent: where the node goes among the parent's children, 0 for first. Default last. Child order is draw order in a CanvasItem and layout order in a Container. Only for ops add, reparent.

instancePath.description: add: a scene to instance as the new node instead of a class, such as "ui/panel.tscn". It is saved as an instance of that file, the way the editor's Instantiate Child Scene saves one, so changes to that scene reach it; properties set its root. A scene that is the target or instances it is refused. Only for op add.

layer.description: set_tilemap_cells: the layer of a TileMap. Default 0. A TileMapLayer is one layer. Only for op set_tilemap_cells.

newName.description: duplicate: the copy's name. Only for op duplicate.

newParentPath.description: reparent: the new parent, which may be the one it has, to move it among its siblings. Only for op reparent.

nodeName.description: add: the new node's name. Only for op add.

nodePath.description: Node path from the scene root, such as "Player/Sprite2D". "." is the root. Only for ops get, set, duplicate, reparent, delete, set_tilemap_cells.

nodeType.description: add: the node class, such as "CharacterBody2D", or a class_name a project script declares, which the node is made as with that script attached. Give this or instancePath. The answer's nodeType is the class of the node made, for an instance the class of its scene's root. Only for op add.

parentNodePath.description: add: where the node goes. Default the root. duplicate: where the copy goes. Only for ops add, duplicate.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

properties.description: Properties to set, keyed by Godot property name. Vectors, colours and the like may be written as {"x": 1, "y": 2} or tagged {"_type": "Vector2", "x": 1, "y": 2}, which is the form a read answers with, so a value read off one node can be written straight to another. One carrying a field its type has not, such as a z for a Vector2, is refused naming it. A colour may also be given as its html code, "#ff8000" or "#ff800080". A key may also be a colon path into one of the components of a vector, a colour, a rectangle or a transform, as GDScript names them, so one axis is written alone: "position:x", "modulate:a", "region_rect:size:y"; a component the value does not have is refused, naming the ones it has. A property holding a node takes the path to it from the node being set, such as "../Player". Each value is read back once set, and one the engine changed or refused is refused with what it holds. An enum property takes the name of a value, as the script spells it, or its number; a value past an export range, or a number no value of an enum has, is written as given and named under outsideDeclared. A whole number of 2^53 or more, such as a 64-bit seed or a resource uid, is written as its digits, {"_type": "int", "value": "9007199254740993"}, the form a read answers with: a JSON number that large can arrive as a neighbour of the one sent, so sent as a number it is refused. Only for ops add, set.

scenePath.description: Scene file inside the project, such as "scenes/main.tscn" or "res://scenes/main.tscn".

name: scene_node
title: Scene nodes
